title: Algebraic spaces are recovered from locally ringed etale topoi
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A ringed-topos morphism is a geometric morphism $u$ with a unital ring-sheaf map $u^\sharp:u^{-1}\mathcal R_Y\to\mathcal R_X$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. A ringed topos is locally ringed if locally every section $a$ has $a$ or $1-a$ invertible, and the equalizer of the sections $0,1$ of its ring sheaf is the initial sheaf. A morphism between locally ringed topoi is local if the square formed by $u^{-1}\mathcal R_Y^\times\to\mathcal R_X^\times$ and $u^{-1}\mathcal R_Y\to\mathcal R_X$ is cartesian. Let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme]. Their small etale topoi with structure sheaves $(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_X)$ and $(\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_Y)$ are locally ringed. Every morphism $h:X\to Y$ induces a local ringed-topos morphism $(h_{\mathrm{et}},h^\sharp)$, compatibly with identities and composition. Every local ringed-topos morphism between these two topoi is isomorphic to the one induced by a unique morphism $h:X\to Y$. Here an isomorphism of ringed-topos morphisms is a natural isomorphism of their inverse-image functors compatible with the ring-sheaf maps. Two space morphisms induce isomorphic ringed-topos morphisms if and only if they are equal, and every automorphism of a ringed-topos morphism induced by a space morphism is the identity. Thus an isomorphism to the induced ringed-topos morphism, when it exists, is unique. No quasi-compactness, separation, or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] each geometric structure-ring stalk is the nonzero local ring given by a strict henselization on an etale scheme chart. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] the geometric stalks preserve finite limits and colimits and detect monomorphisms and epimorphisms. Thus the map $\mathcal O^\times\amalg\mathcal O^\times\to\mathcal O$ given on the two summands by $a\mapsto a$ and $a\mapsto1-a$ is epic: it is surjective in every local-ring stalk. The unit subsheaf is computed by the finite-limit equation $ab=1$, so its stalk is the group of units of the ring stalk. The equalizer of $0,1$ has empty stalks, hence is initial. This proves the stated local-ring conditions for both topoi. For a space morphism $h$, [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] constructs its ringed-topos morphism and [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] identifies its ring stalk maps, and [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] says those maps are local. The comparison from the upper left corner of its unit square to the pullback of the other three corners is bijective at each stalk, hence an isomorphism by [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points]. Thus the morphism is local. The identities and composition comparisons are those of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization].

Fix a local morphism $g$ as in the statement. For etale scheme charts $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ and $s:h_U\to g^{-1}h_V$, [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-slice-functoriality] gives a local ringed morphism of slices. Use [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] to identify these slices with the ringed etale topoi of $U,V$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-ringed-etale-reconstruction] it comes from a unique scheme map $f_s:U\to V$, with a unique ring-compatible two-isomorphism. If $a:U\prime\to U$, $b:V\prime\to V$ and $g^{-1}(b)s\prime=sa$, the functorial square in [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-slice-functoriality] and chart comparison in [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] show that $bf_{s\prime}$ and $f_sa$ induce isomorphic scheme ringed-topos morphisms. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-scheme-ringed-etale-reconstruction] gives $bf_{s\prime}=f_sa$. The corresponding two-isomorphisms agree too: their quotient is an automorphism of this induced scheme morphism, which is the identity by the rigidity clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-ringed-etale-reconstruction].

source.place: Tag 04KL (theorem-fully-faithful), first paragraph and the functoriality square.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its representable sheaf is epic onto the terminal sheaf: any etale scheme over $Y$ is covered by its pullback of this atlas, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The inverse image of a geometric morphism preserves colimits and finite limits, so $g^{-1}h_V\to1$ is epic (an epimorphism is a coequalizer of its kernel pair by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer]). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] to lift the terminal section locally on each chart of an atlas of $X$. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] the resulting family $U_i\to X$ is jointly surjective etale, with $s_i:h_{U_i}\to g^{-1}h_V$. Their disjoint union is a scheme atlas $U\to X$, and the $s_i$ give $s:h_U\to g^{-1}h_V$. Equivalently all the following arguments can be made with this family, avoiding a single disjoint union. Put $R\prime=U\times_XU$ and $R=V\times_YV$. Both are schemes by representability of the diagonals in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Finite-limit preservation gives $g^{-1}h_R=g^{-1}h_V\times g^{-1}h_V$ and hence $s\times s:h_{R\prime}\to g^{-1}h_R$.

source.place: Tag 04KL, choose atlases and form the two relations.

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $(U,V,s)$ and $(R\prime,R,s\times s)$. Functoriality for both projections gives a map of relation diagrams $R\prime\rightrightarrows U$ to $R\rightrightarrows V$. Thus $U\xrightarrow{f_s}V\to Y$ equalizes $R\prime\rightrightarrows U$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] the sheaf quotient of the latter relation is $X$. The universal property of sheafification in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends the resulting quotient-presheaf map uniquely to $h:X\to Y$, with $h|_U$ equal to $V\to Y$ after $f_s$. This is a space morphism because morphisms in [def-trf-algebraic-space] are precisely sheaf natural transformations; no effectiveness theorem for a new algebraic space is needed.

source.place: Tag 04KL, descend the relation diagram to a morphism of spaces.

proof.text: For any sheaf $F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, the two-isomorphism of step 2 on $U,V$ and [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] give $t_U:(h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}F)|_U$. Its two restrictions to $R\prime$ agree: by the last assertion of step 2 both are the comparison obtained from $(R\prime,R,s\times s)$. Work on the enlarged etale site of $X$, which [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] identifies with the small topos; it has terminal object $X$ and all fibre products by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density], and the covering $U\to X$. The map-gluing clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] gives a unique global map $t_F$. Apply it also to $t_U^{-1}$; uniqueness makes the two global maps inverse. For an arrow $F\to G$, the naturality square commutes on $U$ by scheme naturality, hence globally by the uniqueness clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent]. For $F=\mathcal O_Y$, the equality $g^\sharp t_{\mathcal O_Y}=h^\sharp$ likewise holds on $U$ and hence globally. Thus $t$ is the required ring-compatible natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04KL, final paragraph; the omitted descent details use sites.tex Tags 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves) and 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps).

proof.text: For uniqueness, suppose $a,b:X\to Y$ induce ring-compatible isomorphic inverse images $t:a^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}b^{-1}$. Choose a scheme atlas $V\to Y$, pull it back along $a$, and cover $X\times_{Y,a}V$ by an etale scheme atlas; [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [def-trf-algebraic-space] give a scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ and $\alpha:U\to V$ above $a$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] this is a section $c:h_U\to a^{-1}h_V$. The section $t_{h_V}c:h_U\to b^{-1}h_V=h_{X\times_{Y,b}V}$ gives a scheme map $\beta:U\to V$ above $b$: evaluate at the identity of $U$ by [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]. By [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-slice-functoriality] the isomorphism $t$ induces a ring-compatible two-isomorphism between the relocalizations at $c$ and $t_{h_V}c$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] these are the morphisms induced by $\alpha,\beta$. Scheme uniqueness in [lem-sfb-scheme-ringed-etale-reconstruction] gives $\alpha=\beta$. Therefore $ap=bp$, and the quotient description [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] implies $a=b$.

source.place: Tag 04M6 (lemma-faithful), chart reduction and slice two-isomorphism.

proof.text: It remains to prove rigidity, without introducing a node that merely restates that clause. Let $t:h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\to h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ be a ring-compatible natural endomorphism. Fix an affine etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ and a set of $\mathbf Z$-algebra generators $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ of $B$; $J$ may be infinite. The coordinate functions define $h_V\to\prod_j\mathcal O_Y$. After applying $h^{-1}$ to each coordinate and then $h^\sharp$, obtain $$e:h^{-1}h_V=h_{X\times_YV}\longrightarrow\prod_j\mathcal O_X.$$ This is a monomorphism. Indeed, on an etale scheme test $T\to X$, a section on the left is a $Y$-map $T\to V$. Its coordinates are exactly the images of the $b_j$ under $B\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$: the structural map in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] pulls functions back along the projection $T\to V$. Equal coordinates imply equal ring homomorphisms, because the $b_j$ generate $B$ as a $\mathbf Z$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] they imply equal scheme maps $T\to V$ and therefore equal sections. This argument uses the individual coordinate maps and does not assert that $h^{-1}$ preserves an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 04KK (lemma-2-morphism), coordinate embedding; the omitted structural-map verification is spelled out on each scheme test.

proof.text: Naturality of $t$ on the coordinate maps $h_V\to\mathcal O_Y$, and the equation $h^\sharp t_{\mathcal O_Y}=h^\sharp$, give $e\,t_{h_V}=e$ coordinate by coordinate. Since $e$ is monic by step 7, $t_{h_V}=\mathrm{id}$ for every affine etale chart $V$. Every etale scheme is covered by its affine opens by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; these are etale charts by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and chartwise etale permanence [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Subcanonicality in [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-covering-representable-coequalizer-presentation] therefore give, for every sheaf $F$, an epimorphism $P=\coprod h_V\to F$ from affine representables. The left adjoint $h^{-1}$ preserves coproducts and this epimorphism (use its coequalizer presentation). Naturality on all coproduct inclusions makes $t_P=\mathrm{id}$; naturality on $P\to F$ then gives $t_F=\mathrm{id}$. Thus every ring-compatible endomorphism is the identity, in particular every automorphism.

Existence is steps 2--5, and step 6 gives uniqueness of $h$ and equality of any two space morphisms with isomorphic induced ringed morphisms. Equal space morphisms give isomorphic induced ringed morphisms by the identity comparison. If $r,s:g\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{\mathrm{et}}$ are ring-compatible two-isomorphisms, $s r^{-1}$ is an automorphism of the induced ringed morphism, so step 8 makes it the identity and $r=s$. All chart covers above are arbitrary set-indexed covers: no finite subcover, affine intersections, separation, or finiteness assumption was used.
